# MENA Fintech Market Size & Share Analysis - Growth Trends and Forecast (2026 - 2031)
## MENA Fintech Market Trends and Insights
Saudi Arabia targets 70% cashless transactions by 2030, Egypt aims to bank 50% of adults by 2025, and the UAE streamlined licensing in 2024.

Regulatory sandboxes in Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Jordan provide controlled environments for fintech innovation, with SAMA approving multiple neobanking licenses in 2024.

UAE's successful completion of first CBDC payments in 2024 demonstrates technical feasibility and regulatory readiness for broader implementation, creating precedent for regional adoption.

## Geography Analysis
Morocco’s Casablanca Finance City anchored new regulations that fast-track e-money licensing, while Tunisia leverages telco agents to reach rural users.

Jordan’s sandbox routes present a clear regulatory runway, while Lebanon’s diaspora remittances sustain sizable FX flows despite domestic turmoil.

## Regulatory Landscape
In Saudi Arabia, the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) operates an always-open Regulatory Sandbox, and on 26 March 2026 it commenced official licensing of open banking providers.

In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law No. (6) of 2025 took effect on 16 September 2025, broadening the regulatory scope to cover open finance and virtual-asset payment services. In Egypt, the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) issued Decree No 43 on 24 February 2026, suspending new applications for consumer finance company licenses under the FinTech Law for one year, which points to tighter scrutiny in non-bank financial services.
